finding: P2-6 — npm run licenses:check mutates the tracked certification/license-report.json on every run (fresh generatedAt), invalidating recorded artifact hashes
behavior: scripts/check-licenses.mjs computes the report as before and compares the new stable content against the existing certification/license-report.json ignoring volatile top-level fields (generatedAt, timestamp).
If the stable content is equal, the file is not opened for writing (bytes preserved) and the script exits with the same classification exit codes as before.
If the file is missing, unreadable or invalid JSON, it is written (normal path).
If the stable content changed, it is written exactly as before (JSON.stringify report, 2-space indent, trailing newline).
Console event licenses.checked, its fields, and the exit-code rules are unchanged.
--self-test runs deterministic in-process checks in a temp dir and never writes inside the workspace; it is not wired into package.json.

Volatile-field comparison ignores only top-level generatedAt and timestamp (the only volatile fields in schema v2). Any future nested volatile field would count as a content change and trigger a rewrite.

Comparison is semantic (JSON parsed, keys sorted); a semantically-equal but reformatted/key-reordered existing file is preserved byte-for-byte rather than normalized. This is intentional (non-mutating) but means formatting drift in the report is not auto-corrected.
